/-! ### The whole A.3 leg over its honest inputs

`Pic0.isAbelianVariety` (`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean`) states the four conjuncts of the
abelian-variety conclusion, and it consumes `Pic0.proper` and `Pic0.smooth`, i.e. the two
`sorry`s of that file. The theorem below states the same conclusion **plus the dimension**
over the reductions instead, so that the leg's total open content is visible in one signature
and can be checked against a probe rather than read off four docstrings.

Its hypotheses are exactly, and only:

* `hval` — the valuative existence criterion for `(Pic0Scheme C).hom`. This is the *whole* of
  properness (`Pic0.proper_of_valuativeCriterion`; the other three `IsProper` conjuncts are
  theorems of that file, and the ambient-`Pic` route is refuted — `Pic_{C/k}` is an infinite
  disjoint union over `deg ∈ ℤ`, so universal closedness would force `CompactSpace`).
* `hred` — `IsReduced` of the **single** scheme `Pic⁰ ×_{Spec k} Spec k̄`. This is the whole of
  smoothness *and* of geometric reducedness: `Pic0.smooth_of_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange`
  gives smoothness, and `Pic0.geometricallyReduced_of_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange`
  shows the same hypothesis discharges the reducedness obligation too.
* `hid` — the cotangent value at the identity, which is front (a).
* `hreg`, `htrans` — regularity at the identity and the orbit condition, as above.

Nothing else. Geometric irreducibility and the group-object structure are already theorems.
So the A.3 leg is five statements, of which `hid` is the load-bearing one and `hreg` is free
over a perfect field.

**WARNING (run 0067 r8): this theorem is VACUOUS for `g(C) ≥ 1`, because of `htrans`.** It is
true, and its four other hypotheses are the honest content of their respective legs, but
`Pic0.genus_eq_zero_of_homogeneous` (`Picard/HomogeneityOrbitCollapse.lean`) derives
`genus C = 0` from `hid`, `hreg`, `htrans` alone — so on a positive-genus curve the hypothesis
set cannot be satisfied and the conclusion says nothing. Do **not** quote this signature as "the
A.3 leg over its honest inputs": the dimension conjunct is the one that spoils it. The
`IsProper ∧ Smooth ∧ GeometricallyIrreducible ∧ GrpObj` part, over `hval` and `hred` only, is
sound and is the reading to use — see the retraction above the section for what the dimension
half actually needs. -/
theorem isAbelianVariety_of_dimension_genus {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C]
    [PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C]
    [GrpObj (Pic0Scheme C)]
    (hval : ValuativeCriterion.Existence (Pic0Scheme C).hom)
    (hred : IsReduced (Limits.pullback (Pic0Scheme C).hom
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k))))))
    (hid : Module.finrank
        (IsLocalRing.ResidueField ((Pic0Scheme C).left.presheaf.stalk
          ((identitySection C).base default)))
        (IsLocalRing.CotangentSpace ((Pic0Scheme C).left.presheaf.stalk
          ((identitySection C).base default)))
      = AlgebraicGeometry.genus C)
    (hreg : IsRegularLocalRing ((Pic0Scheme C).left.presheaf.stalk
      ((identitySection C).base default)))
    (htrans : ∀ z : (Pic0Scheme C).left,
      ∃ x y : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ Pic0Scheme C,
        (pointTranslationIso (Pic0Scheme C) x y).hom.base
          ((identitySection C).base default) = z) :
    IsProper (Pic0Scheme C).hom ∧ Smooth (Pic0Scheme C).hom ∧
      GeometricallyIrreducible (Pic0Scheme C).hom ∧
      Nonempty (GrpObj (Pic0Scheme C)) ∧
      topologicalKrullDim (Pic0Scheme C).left
        = ((AlgebraicGeometry.genus C : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) :=
  ⟨AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0.proper_of_valuativeCriterion C hval,
   AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0.smooth_of_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange C hred,
   AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0.geometricallyIrreducible C,
   AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0.grpObj C,
   topologicalKrullDim_eq_genus_of_homogeneous C hid hreg htrans⟩

/-- **The A.3 abelian-variety conclusion over its two honest inputs — the NON-VACUOUS
capstone** (run 0067 r8).

`isAbelianVariety_of_dimension_genus` above adds the dimension conjunct, and pays for it with
the orbit condition `htrans`, which is contradictory for `g(C) ≥ 1`
(`Pic0.genus_eq_zero_of_homogeneous`, `Picard/HomogeneityOrbitCollapse.lean`). This theorem is
that statement with the spoiled conjunct and its hypothesis removed: the four defining
abelian-variety properties of Milne §I.1, over

* `hval` — valuative existence, the whole of properness;
* `hred` — `IsReduced` of the **single** scheme `Pic⁰ ×_{Spec k} Spec k̄`, the whole of
  smoothness;

and nothing else. Geometric irreducibility and the group-object structure are theorems of
`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean`. Both hypotheses are satisfiable — neither constrains the
genus — so unlike the five-input form this is the signature to quote for the A.3 leg, with the
dimension statement `dim Pic⁰ = g` tracked separately as still owing the uniform cotangent
bound.

Same caveat as everything in this lane: measure axioms at a SYNTHESIS site. Stated over
`[HasPicScheme C]`, which the caller discharges. -/

    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C]
    [PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C]
    (hval : ValuativeCriterion.Existence (Pic0Scheme C).hom)
    (hred : IsReduced (Limits.pullback (Pic0Scheme C).hom
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k)))))) :
    IsProper (Pic0Scheme C).hom ∧ Smooth (Pic0Scheme C).hom ∧
      GeometricallyIrreducible (Pic0Scheme C).hom ∧
      Nonempty (GrpObj (Pic0Scheme C)) :=
  ⟨AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0.proper_of_valuativeCriterion C hval,
   AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0.smooth_of_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange C hred,

/-! ### The whole A.3 leg over its honest inputs

`Pic0.isAbelianVariety` (`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean`) states the four conjuncts of the
abelian-variety conclusion, and it consumes `Pic0.proper` and `Pic0.smooth`, i.e. the two
`sorry`s of that file. The theorem below states the same conclusion **plus the dimension**
over the reductions instead, so that the leg's total open content is visible in one signature
and can be checked against a probe rather than read off four docstrings.

Its hypotheses are exactly, and only:

* `hval` — the valuative existence criterion for `(Pic0Scheme C).hom`. This is the *whole* of
  properness (`Pic0.proper_of_valuativeCriterion`; the other three `IsProper` conjuncts are
  theorems of that file, and the ambient-`Pic` route is refuted — `Pic_{C/k}` is an infinite
  disjoint union over `deg ∈ ℤ`, so universal closedness would force `CompactSpace`).
* `hred` — `IsReduced` of the **single** scheme `Pic⁰ ×_{Spec k} Spec k̄`. This is the whole of
  smoothness *and* of geometric reducedness: `Pic0.smooth_of_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange`
  gives smoothness, and `Pic0.geometricallyReduced_of_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange`
  shows the same hypothesis discharges the reducedness obligation too.
* `hid` — the cotangent value at the identity, which is front (a).
* `hreg`, `htrans` — regularity at the identity and the orbit condition, as above.

Nothing else. Geometric irreducibility and the group-object structure are already theorems.
So the A.3 leg is five statements, of which `hid` is the load-bearing one and `hreg` is free
over a perfect field.

**WARNING (run 0067 r8): this theorem is VACUOUS for `g(C) ≥ 1`, because of `htrans`.** It is
true, and its four other hypotheses are the honest content of their respective legs, but
`Pic0.genus_eq_zero_of_homogeneous` (`Picard/HomogeneityOrbitCollapse.lean`) derives
`genus C = 0` from `hid`, `hreg`, `htrans` alone — so on a positive-genus curve the hypothesis
set cannot be satisfied and the conclusion says nothing. Do **not** quote this signature as "the
A.3 leg over its honest inputs": the dimension conjunct is the one that spoils it. The
`IsProper ∧ Smooth ∧ GeometricallyIrreducible ∧ GrpObj` part, over `hval` and `hred` only, is
sound and is the reading to use — see the retraction above the section for what the dimension
half actually needs. -/
theorem isAbelianVariety_of_dimension_genus {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C]
    [PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C]
    [GrpObj (Pic0Scheme C)]
    (hval : ValuativeCriterion.Existence (Pic0Scheme C).hom)
    (hred : IsReduced (Limits.pullback (Pic0Scheme C).hom
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k))))))
    (hid : Module.finrank
        (IsLocalRing.ResidueField ((Pic0Scheme C).left.presheaf.stalk
          ((identitySection C).base default)))
        (IsLocalRing.CotangentSpace ((Pic0Scheme C).left.presheaf.stalk
          ((identitySection C).base default)))
      = AlgebraicGeometry.genus C)
    (hreg : IsRegularLocalRing ((Pic0Scheme C).left.presheaf.stalk
      ((identitySection C).base default)))
    (htrans : ∀ z : (Pic0Scheme C).left,
      ∃ x y : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ Pic0Scheme C,
        (pointTranslationIso (Pic0Scheme C) x y).hom.base
          ((identitySection C).base default) = z) :
    IsProper (Pic0Scheme C).hom ∧ Smooth (Pic0Scheme C).hom ∧
      GeometricallyIrreducible (Pic0Scheme C).hom ∧
      Nonempty (GrpObj (Pic0Scheme C)) ∧
      topologicalKrullDim (Pic0Scheme C).left
        = ((AlgebraicGeometry.genus C : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) :=
  ⟨AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0.proper_of_valuativeCriterion C hval,
   AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0.smooth_of_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange C hred,
   AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0.geometricallyIrreducible C,
   AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0.grpObj C,
   topologicalKrullDim_eq_genus_of_homogeneous C hid hreg htrans⟩

/-- **The A.3 abelian-variety conclusion over its two honest inputs — the NON-VACUOUS
capstone** (run 0067 r8).

`isAbelianVariety_of_dimension_genus` above adds the dimension conjunct, and pays for it with
the orbit condition `htrans`, which is contradictory for `g(C) ≥ 1`
(`Pic0.genus_eq_zero_of_homogeneous`, `Picard/HomogeneityOrbitCollapse.lean`). This theorem is
that statement with the spoiled conjunct and its hypothesis removed: the four defining
abelian-variety properties of Milne §I.1, over

* `hval` — valuative existence, the whole of properness;
* `hred` — `IsReduced` of the **single** scheme `Pic⁰ ×_{Spec k} Spec k̄`, the whole of
  smoothness;

and nothing else. Geometric irreducibility and the group-object structure are theorems of
`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean`. Both hypotheses are satisfiable — neither constrains the
genus — so unlike the five-input form this is the signature to quote for the A.3 leg, with the
dimension statement `dim Pic⁰ = g` tracked separately as still owing the uniform cotangent
bound.

Same caveat as everything in this lane: measure axioms at a SYNTHESIS site. Stated over
`[HasPicScheme C]`, which the caller discharges. -/
theorem isAbelianVariety_of_valuative_of_isReduced {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C]
    [PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C]
    (hval : ValuativeCriterion.Existence (Pic0Scheme C).hom)
    (hred : IsReduced (Limits.pullback (Pic0Scheme C).hom
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (AlgebraicClosure k)))))) :
    IsProper (Pic0Scheme C).hom ∧ Smooth (Pic0Scheme C).hom ∧
      GeometricallyIrreducible (Pic0Scheme C).hom ∧
      Nonempty (GrpObj (Pic0Scheme C)) :=
  ⟨AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0.proper_of_valuativeCriterion C hval,
   AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0.smooth_of_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange C hred,
   AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0.geometricallyIrreducible C,
   AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0.grpObj C⟩

11	Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.smooth_of_grpObj` proves that a group scheme locally of finite
12	type over a field is smooth as soon as it is **geometrically** reduced, i.e. as soon as
13	`X ×_k Spec K` is reduced for *every* field `K` and every `Spec K ⟶ Spec k`. Internally it
14	goes through a `private` lemma which needs only reducedness of the **single** base change to
15	the algebraic closure — the geometric content is the translation argument at an algebraically
16	closed base, and the general field case is obtained by flat descent along `Spec k̄ → Spec k`.
17	
18	That `private` modifier is the whole reason for this file. Both this project and the sibling
19	`Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` reached the same conclusion independently (inbox
20	I-0495, 2026-07-28): the smoothness leg of "`Pic⁰_{C/k}` is an abelian variety" wants to
21	supply reducedness over `k̄` and nothing more, because
22	
23	* `Algebra.IsGeometricallyReduced` is *defined* by base change to an algebraic closure
24	  (`Mathlib/RingTheory/Nilpotent/GeometricallyReduced.lean`), so at the algebra level the
25	  k̄-statement is the definition rather than a special case;
26	* the scheme-level class `GeometricallyReduced` quantifies over all field base changes, and
27	  the passage from the `k̄` case to that quantifier is **absent from mathlib v4.31** — it is
28	  the transcendental half of `IsReduced after base change to k̄ ⟹ GeometricallyReduced`,
29	  which has no producer in mathlib and no `MorphismProperty.DescendsAlong` instance either
30	  (verified by machine on both sides, recorded on inbox I-0495).
31	
32	So the honest input to smoothness is the `k̄` one, and the cross-project thread priced getting
33	it as *an upstream PR making `smooth_of_grpObj_of_isAlgClosed` public*. It is cheaper than
34	that: the `private` proof uses only public API, so it can simply be re-derived here. This
35	file does that and then packages the descent step, giving a smoothness criterion whose
36	hypothesis is a single `IsReduced`.
37	
38	## Main results
39	
40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.smooth_of_grpObj_of_isAlgClosed'` — the re-derivation of mathlib's
41	  `private` lemma: a reduced group scheme locally of finite type over an algebraically closed
42	  field is smooth. Proof transcribed from `Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Group/Smooth.lean`
43	  (Andrew Yang), which is why the `set_option`s and the `open`s are the same.
44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.smooth_of_grpObj_of_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange` — the
45	  criterion this project actually consumes: `G ⟶ Spec k` is smooth as soon as the base change
46	  `G ×_{Spec k} Spec k̄` is reduced. No `GeometricallyReduced`, no quantifier over fields.
47	
48	## Change of attack surface, NOT of strength — corrected after review
49	
50	An earlier version of this docstring called the criterion's hypothesis **strictly weaker** than
51	`smooth_of_grpObj`'s. **That is wrong in this project, and the correction is the interesting
52	part.** Fresh-context review (run 0067) established:
53	
54	* in **mathlib alone**, `IsReduced`-over-`k̄ ⟹ GeometricallyReduced` is indeed unavailable —
55	  `infer_instance` fails for it on a bare `import Mathlib`;
56	* but **this project owns the converse**: `Smooth.geometricallyReduced`
57	  (`AlgebraicJacobian/Curve/GeometricallyReduced.lean`, an instance) derives the class from
58	  smoothness. So `IsReduced`-over-`k̄` → (this criterion) → `Smooth` → `GeometricallyReduced`
59	  closes by `inferInstance`, axiom-clean.
60	
61	At these binders the two hypotheses are therefore **interprovable**, and this file is a
62	restatement rather than a weakening. The mistake was methodological and worth recording: the
63	"missing in mathlib" measurement was taken inside the *edited file's* import cone (99 modules),
64	which does not contain `Curve/GeometricallyReduced`, while the root cone (215 modules) does.
65	A synthesis probe cannot see a bridge its own imports exclude — measure at the root.
66	
67	**What the restatement is still good for**, which is why it stays: the two hypotheses are
68	equivalent but not equally *attackable*. `GeometricallyReduced` quantifies over every field
69	extension and has no producer here other than the circular one; reducedness of one scheme over
70	one algebraically closed field is where Kleiman §5's argument (and Cartier's theorem in
71	characteristic zero) actually speaks. Same strength, better attack surface.
72	
73	**And the corollary the first version missed**: since the criterion yields `Smooth` and
74	`Smooth.geometricallyReduced` yields the class, the `k̄` hypothesis discharges
75	`Pic0.geometricallyReduced` — an open `sorry` of `Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` — as well as
76	the smoothness leg. One statement, two obligations. Verified axiom-clean at the root; see
77	`Pic0.geometricallyReduced_of_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange` there.

9	# Universal closedness is incompatible with an infinite disjoint cover
10	
11	## Why this file exists: a landed reduction of this project reduced nothing
12	
13	`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` carries two theorems that move properness of
14	`Pic⁰_{C/k}` onto the **ambient** Picard scheme:
15	
16	* `Pic0.universallyClosed_of_ambient` — `UniversallyClosed (PicScheme C).hom`
17	  implies `UniversallyClosed (Pic0Scheme C).hom`, because `Pic⁰ ↪ Pic` is a
18	  *closed* immersion;
19	* `Pic0.proper_of_ambient_universallyClosed` — hence properness of `Pic⁰`.
20	
21	Both are true, sorry-free and axiom-clean, and the roadmap row
22	`AJC.pic0av.structure` recommended that route as "a SECOND, INDEPENDENT reduction
23	… worth trying first", on the reading that Kleiman §5 Thm.~`th:qpp&p` is a
24	theorem about `Pic_{C/k}` and so the ambient object is where the argument lives.
25	
26	**The hypothesis those two theorems consume cannot hold.** `UniversallyClosed` is
27	strictly stronger than one expects over an affine base: mathlib derives
28	`QuasiCompact` from it (`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/UniversallyClosed.lean`,
29	the `priority := 900` instance — this is exactly *why* `IsProper` has only three
30	fields and omits quasi-compactness), and `Spec R` is a compact space, so
31	`QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace` upgrades it to `CompactSpace X`.
32	
33	But `Pic_{C/k}` is a **disjoint union over `deg ∈ ℤ`** — that is the second clause
34	of Kleiman §4 Thm.~`th:main`(1), the very clause `HasPicScheme` bundles ("a
35	disjoint union of open quasi-projective `k`-subschemes"). An infinite family of
36	pairwise disjoint nonempty opens covering a space has no finite subcover. So
37	`Pic_{C/k}` is not quasi-compact, hence not universally closed, and
38	`universallyClosed_of_ambient` is an instance of **trap (c)**: a `P → Q` whose
39	antecedent is unsatisfiable in the intended setting. It passes every axiom probe
40	and every `sorry` census, because it is a theorem.
41	
42	## What this file adds, and what survives
43	
44	The three results below are the general statements, at scheme generality and with
45	no Picard vocabulary, that make the refutation checkable rather than argued:
46	
47	* `not_compactSpace_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover` — pure topology.
48	* `Scheme.compactSpace_of_universallyClosed` — the mathlib chain, as one name.
49	* `Scheme.not_universallyClosed_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover` — the two
50	  composed: a scheme with an infinite disjoint open cover is not universally
51	  closed over an affine base.
52	
53	`Scheme.not_isProper_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover` records the same conclusion
54	for `IsProper`, since `UniversallyClosed` is one of its fields.
55	
56	**What survives untouched.** The properness route through `Pic⁰` *itself*:
57	`Pic0.proper_of_valuativeCriterion` and
58	`Pic0.universallyClosed_of_valuativeCriterion` quantify over
59	`(Pic0Scheme C).hom`, whose source **is** quasi-compact (`Pic0.quasiCompact`,
60	landed run 0009 from Kleiman §5 Lem.~`lem:agps`(3)), so nothing here touches
61	them. The same holds for `Pic0.universallyClosed_of_baseChange`: base change to
62	`k̄` does not leave the identity component. What the roadmap called the fallback
63	was in fact the only route, and the "second, independent reduction" was never a
64	reduction.
65	
66	Note this says nothing against `Pic0.universallyClosed_of_ambient` as a
67	*theorem*, and it is retained: if some future development produces a single
68	`Pic^d` or a finite union as the ambient object, the closed-immersion transport
69	is exactly right. It is the *satisfiability* at `PicScheme C` that fails.
70	-/
71	
72	universe u v
73	
74	open AlgebraicGeometry CategoryTheory Set
75	
76	/-- **An infinite disjoint open cover obstructs compactness.** If a space is
77	covered by an infinite family of pairwise disjoint *nonempty* opens, it is not
78	compact: a finite subcover omits some index `j`, and any point of `U j` then lies
79	in some `U i` with `i ≠ j`, contradicting disjointness.
80	
81	Nonemptiness is essential (an infinite family of copies of `∅` covers nothing and
82	obstructs nothing), and so is disjointness — without it a finite subfamily can
83	perfectly well cover. -/
84	theorem not_compactSpace_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover
85	    {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] {ι : Type v} [Infinite ι]
86	    (U : ι → Set X) (hopen : ∀ i, IsOpen (U i)) (hne : ∀ i, (U i).Nonempty)
87	    (hdisj : Pairwise (Function.onFun Disjoint U))
88	    (hcov : (univ : Set X) ⊆ ⋃ i, U i) :
89	    ¬ CompactSpace X := by
90	  intro _
91	  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := (CompactSpace.isCompact_univ (X := X)).elim_finite_subcover U hopen hcov
92	  obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := Infinite.exists_notMem_finset t
93	  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := hne j
94	  obtain ⟨i, hi, hxi⟩ := Set.mem_iUnion₂.mp (ht (Set.mem_univ x))
95	  exact (hdisj (fun hh : i = j => hj (hh ▸ hi))).le_bot ⟨hxi, hx⟩
96	
97	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
98	
99	/-- **Universal closedness over an affine base forces a compact space.**
100	
101	The chain, all mathlib: `UniversallyClosed f` gives `QuasiCompact f` (the
102	`priority := 900` instance of `Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/UniversallyClosed.lean`
103	— the reason `IsProper` omits a quasi-compactness field), `Spec R` is a compact
104	space (`PrimeSpectrum.compactSpace`), and a quasi-compact morphism to a compact
105	base has compact source (`QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace`).
106	
107	Stated as its own name because the implication is easy to miss and it is what
108	refutes the ambient-Picard properness route: `UniversallyClosed` is *not* merely
109	"closed under all base changes", it carries finiteness of the source. -/
110	theorem compactSpace_of_universallyClosed {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {X : Scheme.{u}}
111	    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R)) [UniversallyClosed f] : CompactSpace X :=
112	  QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace f
113	
114	/-- **A scheme with an infinite disjoint open cover is not universally closed over
115	an affine base.** Composite of `compactSpace_of_universallyClosed` with
116	`not_compactSpace_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover`.
117	
118	This is the checkable form of the refutation described in this file's header: it
119	applies to `Pic_{C/k}`, whose decomposition into the degree pieces `Pic^d` for
120	`d ∈ ℤ` is a cover of exactly this shape (Kleiman §4 Thm.~`th:main`(1)). Supplying
121	that decomposition as an actual `ℤ`-indexed family of opens is a separate
122	obligation, and this project does **not** have it: it has the degree map
123	(`PicScheme.degree`) but no fibrewise decomposition of the *scheme*. So this file
124	deliberately stops at the general statement and does not assert the instance at
125	`PicScheme C`; what it establishes is that the ambient route is
126	unsatisfiable-in-principle, which is enough to retract it as a reduction. -/
127	theorem not_universallyClosed_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover
128	    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R))
129	    {ι : Type v} [Infinite ι] (U : ι → Set X) (hopen : ∀ i, IsOpen (U i))
130	    (hne : ∀ i, (U i).Nonempty) (hdisj : Pairwise (Function.onFun Disjoint U))
131	    (hcov : (univ : Set X) ⊆ ⋃ i, U i) :
132	    ¬ UniversallyClosed f := fun _ =>
133	  not_compactSpace_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover U hopen hne hdisj hcov
134	    (compactSpace_of_universallyClosed f)
135	
136	/-- **The same obstruction for `IsProper`.** `UniversallyClosed` is a field of
137	`IsProper` (`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/Proper.lean`), so a scheme with
138	an infinite disjoint open cover is not proper over an affine base either — no
139	separatedness or finite-type input is used. -/
140	theorem not_isProper_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover
141	    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R))
142	    {ι : Type v} [Infinite ι] (U : ι → Set X) (hopen : ∀ i, IsOpen (U i))
143	    (hne : ∀ i, (U i).Nonempty) (hdisj : Pairwise (Function.onFun Disjoint U))
144	    (hcov : (univ : Set X) ⊆ ⋃ i, U i) :
145	    ¬ IsProper f := fun h =>
146	  not_universallyClosed_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover f U hopen hne hdisj hcov
147	    h.toUniversallyClosed
148	
149	end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
